name: Ngkolmpu
confidence_why: Carroll's 2016 reference grammar and his 2021 phonology chapter, the only first-hand descriptions of Ngkolmpu, mark stress on transcribed words but never state where it falls or what kind of system it is, and no other source (Donohue 2013, Evans 2021) fills the gap, so the record stands as undetermined on one describer's silence with nothing against it.
catalog_citation: Carroll, Matthew J. 2016. The Ngkolmpu Language with special reference to distributed exponence. PhD thesis, Australian National University (ANU Open Research, handle 1885/116801). Checked against: Carroll, Matthew J. 2021. Phonetics and phonology of Ngkolmpu…
catalog_locator: Carroll 2016: Ch. 2 Phonology pp. 27-56 has no stress/prosody section (TOC 2.1-2.6); prose stress mentions only sec. 3.1 p. 65 (prefix <o>), sec. 4 bare-noun m…
catalog_quote: This chapter sets out the phonemic inventory of consonants (2.1) and vowels (2.2) and describes their distribution and phonetic realisation. It establishes a set of phonotactic constraints (2.4) which are organised around a phonetic syllable structure. This structure is essential for describing the extensive process of epenthesis (2.4.1). The chapter also sets out the morphophonemic processes which interact with the phonotactics (2.5). The chapter concludes with a discussion of the orthography (2.6). ... [p. 65, infinitive prefix <o>] It is typically quite short and always unstressed. ... There is both phonological and syntactic evidence that these are not morphological compounds. Firstly, these are two distinct phonological units with individual stress for each word. ... The clitic never attracts stress and occurs within the intonation contour of the verb.

tone_statements.quote: Reflecting on the diversity of the region on the phonological level, it is difficult to identify any typological features of the phonologies of Southern New Guinea, other than absences (e.g., no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama, no ejectives etc.).
tone_statements.locator: p.7 (third page of the chapter, paragraph after the Urama pitch accent remark)
tone_statements.summary: Areal/comparative statement: no tone and no pitch accent in the SNG sample, which includes the Kanum variety Ngkolmpu; Urama (Kiwaian) alone has pitch accent.

sources.note: Areal overview of the eight languages in LD&C SP24 (Yelmek, Ngkolmpu, Nmbo, Nen, Idi, Ende, Bitur, Urama); Sota Kanum [krz] is not in the sample -- the Kanum-group language covered is Ngkontar Ngkolmpu [kcd, ngka1235] (Glottolog: Yam > Kanum > Ngkrn-Ngkantr > Ngkantr; Sota Kanum sits directly under Ngkrn-Ngkantr). P.7 states that SNG phonologies share no positive typological features, only absences: 'no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama'. Bears on Sota Kanum only as sister-language/areal evidence.
